intended_object: The universal property of K₀(R) as the group completion of the monoid of isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective R-modules: additive maps from that monoid to an abelian group G correspond bijectively to group homomorphisms K₀(R) → G. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The library defines `K0 R` as `Algebra.GrothendieckAddGroup (ProjectiveClass R)`, the Grothendieck group of the monoid of direct-sum isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective (right) R-modules. `lift` is Mathlib's general bijection `Algebra.GrothendieckAddGroup.lift : (M →+ G) ≃ (GrothendieckAddGroup M →+ G)` applied to this monoid. Its inverse is precomposition with the canonical map, as `lift_symm_apply` records. So it is exactly the universal property of the group completion, applied to K₀(R), with the target G an arbitrary abelian group in any universe. It is a specialization of a general Mathlib construction, but only because it is about the specific object K₀(R). The general version is used directly, not rewritten in a narrower setting, so the definition is not too narrow.
